title: Mortality factors declare age basis, conditional interval and terminal support
question: Compare attained-age indexes, fractional-death assumptions, survival/decrement precision, reversed factors, terminal support and validation without treating every numeric table as probabilities.

evidence.title: Reversed survival is an inverse factor, not a probability
explanation: Reversed survival intervals return reciprocal factors; reversed decrements are transformed using survival rather than simply negated. Empty forward reductions return survival one and decrement zero.
The source defines backward factors, which need not be probabilities bounded by one. Zero-survival reversal also has a singular numeric boundary.

Explicit interpolation/model, admissible ages, and nonzero survival when a reciprocal is required. A reversed survival factor may exceed one and its decrement may be negative; this alone is not an invalid probability claim about a forward interval. No upstream execution. evidence.title: Mortality support ending does not establish extinction
explanation: LifeContingencies adds one year to a rate vector last age when forming life horizon, but not to a parametric law omega. Whole-life products reject infinite support without explicit term and reject continuation past an incomplete finite assumption while lives remain active. Endowment supplies an explicit maturity. This differs from simply truncating expectation at the last model age.

Static source and selected product tests only; no independent actuarial or statutory acceptance. Parametric constructor admits issue ages without comparing omega locally; downstream support checks remain relevant.

evidence.title: Observed single-life status and joint-status conditioning differ
explanation: SingleLife one-time survival honors alive atissue, while two-time form asks hypothetical mortality conditional on being alive atfrom. Joint two-time survival instead divides aggregate active-to by active-from and rejects zero conditioning mass. Independent joint states are Cartesian products, with LastSurvivor any-alive and FirstToDie all-alive; observed named state is a distinct valuation input.
Same source/dependency family, not independent corroboration. Rate validity and caller mortality basis remain external inputs; no claim that independence is appropriate for a real portfolio.
